exposure: Non-spontaneous late preterm delivery (categorized as evidence-based vs. non-evidence-based criteria)
Indications for non-spontaneous LPT delivery (severe preeclampsia, abnormal fetal tracing, hemorrhage, mild preeclampsia)
cohort: The study included 2017 late preterm neonates (born between 34 0/7 and 36 6/7 gestational weeks) from 40,609 singleton live births at a Swiss university maternity unit.
finding: Late preterm birth rates remained stable over time, but neonatal complications stayed high, especially after non-evidence-indicated late preterm births, suggesting that 287 late preterm births could have been avoided.
